title: Sable and the Compass
premise: Riverboat captain Ulyana Nystrom inherits a dying prospector's map and a promise to deliver it to his estranged daughter in the high mining town of Kestrel Gap. Pursued by the prospector's former partners, who want the map's claim erased along with anyone who knows of it, Ulyana and her reluctant crew abandon the river for a brutal overland crossing ahead of the early snows. Along the way, the compass the prospector gave her begins pointing not north but toward truths she has spent years avoiding — about the debt that owns her boat, the fire that took her family, and her own complicity in it. At Kestrel Gap, Ulyana must choose between paying her debt with the map's secret or honoring the promise, and she chooses truth: she delivers the map, exposes the partners, and surrenders the boat, walking out of the mountains with nothing but the compass — finally pointing home.
about_author: Orsen Amberdale is the pen name of a former barge hand who spent six seasons on northern waterways before turning to writing. Their fiction is known for spare prose, weather as antagonist, and characters who lie to themselves until the landscape won't let them.

chapters.title: The Mood of the Water
chapters.summary: Ulyana pilots the Sable Queen down a low, treacherous stretch of river, establishing her mastery of the sandbars and her crushing debt to freight magnate Corvin Hale. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: pride shadowed by entrapment; she loves the river because it's the only thing that hasn't been taken from her.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Landing
chapters.summary: At a muddy landing, a feverish old prospector named Ede Voss begs passage. Ulyana refuses payment but takes him aboard out of habit rather than kindness. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: guarded compassion; she recognizes a drowning man because she's been one.

chapters.title: What Ede Carried
chapters.summary: Ede raves about a silver lode and a daughter named Ingrid he abandoned twenty years ago. Crew member Tamir finds a wrapped bundle in Ede's gear — a map and an odd brass compass. POV: Tamir. Emotional beat: temptation; Tamir, who dreams of leaving the boat, sees escape in the bundle.

chapters.title: The Dying Trade
chapters.summary: Ede, near death, offers Ulyana the map in exchange for one promise: carry it to Ingrid Voss in Kestrel Gap before the passes close. Ulyana hesitates — Kestrel Gap is weeks away and wrong direction entirely. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the weight of being asked to be trustworthy when she doesn't trust herself.

chapters.title: Men on the Bank
chapters.summary: Two riders watch the Sable Queen from shore — agents of Ede's former partners, the Aldous brothers, who sold his claim rights and now need the map destroyed. That night they board, searching. POV: Tamir. Emotional beat: first real fear; the adventure stops being hypothetical.

chapters.title: Ede's Last Morning
chapters.summary: Ede dies at dawn, pressing the compass into Ulyana's hand with words about 'true bearing' that seem to mean more than navigation. The Aldouses demand the dead man's effects; Ulyana lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve — the promise is made, and she keeps promises badly but absolutely.

chapters.title: Hale's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corvin Hale intercepts the boat, offering to forgive Ulyana's debt if she hands over whatever Ede carried — the Aldouses have already paid him. Ulyana refuses, and Hale gives her until the snows to reconsider. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: cornered defiance; loyalty to a dead man over her own survival.

chapters.title: Abandoning the River
chapters.summary: Ulyana moors the Sable Queen at a trusted friend's dock and leads her small crew — Tamir and cook Marta — onto the overland trail to Kestrel Gap. The compass behaves strangely, drifting off north. POV: Tamir. Emotional beat: grief for the boat mixed with exhilaration; leaving everything familiar.

chapters.title: The Low Pass
chapters.summary: The trio crosses foothills, outrunning word of their route. They discover the Aldouses have hired local trackers; a near-capture in a market town forces them to split and regroup. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: Marta's dry courage steadies the group; found-family bonds tighten under pressure.

chapters.title: The Compass Turns
chapters.summary: Camped high, Ulyana realizes the compass needle points not north but steadily toward a valley she recognizes — the site of the fire that killed her family fifteen years ago, a fire tied to a Hale contract. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: dread and vertigo; memory she has buried begins demanding interest.

chapters.title: What Ulyana Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Ulyana, working for Hale, delivered the lantern oil that started the fire — told it was empty warehouses. It wasn't. She has never spoken of it. POV: Ulyana (past and present interwoven). Emotional beat: shame surfacing; identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Tamir's Bargain
chapters.summary: Tamir, terrified and tempted, secretly contacts the Aldouses, offering the map's location for money. He can't go through with it, but they've seen his face. POV: Tamir. Emotional beat: betrayal aborted but not undone; loyalty tested and found wanting.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: Early snow catches them on an exposed shoulder of the range. They shelter in a prospector's ruined cabin where Ede once lived; scratched on the wall are his notes — including mention of Hale by name. POV: Marta. Emotional beat: the past closing in literally; the mountain strips them to essentials.

chapters.title: The Aldouses Close In
chapters.summary: The brothers ambush them at a river ford. In the fight, Marta is injured and Tamir confesses his contact with the enemy. Ulyana spares the younger Aldous brother when she has him at her mercy. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: mercy as choice, not weakness; forgiveness extended before it's earned.

chapters.title: Ingrid Voss, Found Early
chapters.summary: By chance they meet a survey party led by Ingrid Voss herself, descending to winter quarters. Hardened and bitter, Ingrid refuses the map: 'He was nothing to me.' POV: Ingrid. Emotional beat: the promise's destination rejecting delivery; grief wearing anger's clothes.

chapters.title: The Needle and the Fire
chapters.summary: Ulyana tells Ingrid the truth about her own past — the fire, Hale, her silence — as proof that secrets rot. Ingrid softens enough to take the map unread. The compass needle steadies, pointing true north for the first time. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: confession as liberation; the theme crystallizes — truth costs less than carried lies.

chapters.title: Kestrel Gap
chapters.summary: They reach Kestrel Gap through the storm only to find Hale waiting, having bought the town's debts including Ulyana's. He offers the same trade publicly: the map for her freedom. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: the trap fully sprung; every thread converging.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Before witnesses, Ingrid opens the map — and reveals it documents not just silver but the Aldouses' fraudulent seizure of Ede's original claim, with Hale's signature as witness. The map is evidence, not treasure. POV: Ingrid. Emotional beat: reversal; the inheritance is justice, and the hunters become the hunted.

chapters.title: Settlement
chapters.summary: The mining camp's council voids the fraudulent claims; the Aldouses flee; Hale's leverage collapses as his witness fraud surfaces. Ulyana's debt dies with his legitimacy — but so does the Sable Queen, seized as collateral in the chaos. POV: Tamir. Emotional beat: victory with a price; the law moves slower than hope but arrives.

chapters.title: What the Boat Was Worth
chapters.summary: Ulyana grieves the Sable Queen properly, standing on the frozen riverbank. Marta and Tamir choose to stay with her rather than take offered berths. Ingrid asks, almost shyly, what Ede was like at the end. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: mourning and gratitude braided together; identity rebuilt without the boat.

chapters.title: Spring Water
chapters.summary: Months later, thaw. Ingrid works the legitimate claim; Ulyana, Tamir, and Marta sign onto a new vessel — smaller, theirs in partnership. The compass hangs at Ulyana's neck, pointing north like any honest instrument. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: quiet renewal; she carries less now, and it weighs less.

chapters.title: True Bearing
chapters.summary: On the new boat's maiden run, Ulyana navigates a sandbar she's known for years and greets it like an old friend. A passenger asks about the compass; she says it belonged to a man who kept his last promise. So did she. POV: Ulyana. Emotional beat: wholeness; the story closes on identity reconciled — captain, keeper of promises, survivor.
